title: README Design Fiction: Beacon Story Creation
description:
# Objective
Create a new design fiction that tells the story of Saturn Beacons in an engaging way, similar to how Derek and Sarah's story introduces Saturn. This design fiction should explain the beacon vision and implementation in narrative form.

# Source Materials
Review these files to understand the beacon implementation and vision:
- beacons/ directory (all files)
- clients/simple_chat_client.py (beacon discovery implementation)
- anchors/Saturn_Winter_Memo.md (the grand vision)
- anchors/Sprint1_Implementation_Plan.md (technical implementation details)

# Current Design Fiction Reference
The existing README has Derek and Sarah's story (lines 9-28). Use this as a style guide for tone, pacing, and engagement level.

# Deliverables
Write a compelling design fiction that:
1. Introduces a relatable character/scenario
2. Explains the problem that beacons solve (credential management, network-based access)
3. Shows how beacons work through the character's experience
4. Conveys the technical vision without getting bogged down in implementation details
5. Maintains the same engaging, slightly humorous tone as Derek/Sarah story
6. Accurately reflects what beacons actually do (ephemeral credentials, mDNS discovery, time-limited access)

# Guidelines
- Keep it concise (similar length to Derek/Sarah story)
- Make it technically accurate but narratively engaging
- Don't sacrifice clarity for cleverness
- Ensure it flows naturally into technical documentation

# Completion Instructions
When this issue is complete:
1. STOP and notify the user
2. Tell the user to run /commit to save this work
3. Inform the user that the next issue to work on is merging the design fictions

# Notes
- This is independent from technical planning (can be done in parallel)
- The design fiction should inspire readers while educating them
- Think: "How would you explain beacons to a skeptical developer at a conference?"

title: Sprint 1 Retrospective: Strip beacon to core requirements
description: Adam's feedback: The beacon's entire job is to (1) generate ephemeral JWT from DeepInfra, (2) announce it via mDNS, and (3) rotate every 5 minutes. The FastAPI server is dead weight - clients extract keys from mDNS and call DeepInfra directly, so there's no HTTP traffic to the beacon at all. FastAPI, uvicorn, /v1/health, and /v1/models should be removed. Target: reduce from ~280 lines to ~150 lines, remove two dependencies, accurately reflect 'a script that announces how to access some other service.'

title: Remove FastAPI and uvicorn from beacon implementation
description: Strip out the entire FastAPI app (lines 233-268 in deepinfra_beacon.py): remove app instance, /v1/health endpoint, /v1/models endpoint. Remove uvicorn.run() call from main(). The beacon should be a standalone script that runs rotation_loop in the foreground or as a daemon, not a web server.

title: Refactor main() to run rotation loop without web server
description: After removing FastAPI/uvicorn, refactor main() to run rotation_loop directly. Options: (1) run rotation_loop in main thread with while True loop, or (2) keep daemon thread but add signal.pause() or similar to block main thread. Must maintain clean shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The beacon should just run forever rotating keys and updating mDNS, nothing more.

title: Update beacon documentation to reflect simplified architecture
description: Update beacons/README.md to remove all references to FastAPI server, /v1/health endpoint, /v1/models endpoint, and uvicorn. Update architecture section (line 12 currently says 'FastAPI server that coordinates all components'). Update 'Endpoints' section (lines 107-113) - either remove entirely or note that beacon has no HTTP endpoints. Update prerequisites to remove fastapi and uvicorn from pip install command.

title: Validate simplified beacon works with existing clients
description: After stripping FastAPI/uvicorn, manually test that simplified beacon still works correctly with EXISTING files: clients/simple_chat_client.py and tests/test_beacon_flow.py. No new test files. Clients should still be able to: (1) discover beacon via mDNS, (2) extract ephemeral_key from TXT records, (3) make successful API calls to DeepInfra, (4) detect key rotation via update_service() callbacks. All Sprint 1 success criteria must still pass.

title: Document implications for future beacon features
description: Create a brief design note about when/if we'd add FastAPI back. Adam says 'If you later need health checks or endpoints, you can add them back.' Document what would trigger that decision: Layer 2 (metering/budgeting)? Layer 3 (agent coordination)? Or would those be separate services? This ensures we don't repeat the mistake of prematurely adding infrastructure for hypothetical future needs.

title: README Review: Begrudging Programmer Perspective
description:
# Objective
Read the README as a begrudging programmer who doesn't like cheesiness and just wants to understand the codebase. Verify that the design fiction hasn't gone overboard and that technical content remains accessible to skeptical, no-nonsense developers.

# Dependencies
- MUST complete Saturn-4lc (technical verification)

# Persona
You are a senior developer who:
- Has seen too many overhyped projects
- Values clarity over cleverness
- Wants to understand "what does this actually do?" immediately
- Dislikes marketing speak and excessive storytelling
- Appreciates good documentation but has zero patience for fluff
- Will abandon the README if it wastes their time

# Review Criteria
1. Can you find installation instructions quickly?
2. Are technical concepts explained clearly without narrative detours?
3. Does the design fiction add value or just take up space?
4. Can you understand the architecture without reading the stories?
5. Are code examples immediately accessible?
6. Is there a clear "quick start" path?
7. Does the README respect your time?

# Specific Checks
- Ratio check: Is storytelling consuming more than 35% of the content?
- Skip test: Can someone skip the design fiction and still understand everything?
- Clarity test: Are technical explanations self-contained?
- Time-to-value: How many lines until useful information appears?
- Jargon check: Is there unnecessary marketing language?

# Deliverables
1. Identify sections where design fiction overshadows technical content
2. Flag any storytelling that doesn't serve a clear educational purpose
3. Recommend cuts or condensing of narrative elements
4. Ensure there's a fast path for impatient developers
5. Verify that design fiction enhances rather than obscures

# Balance Target
- Design fiction should be engaging but skippable
- Technical content should stand on its own
- Stories should teach concepts, not just entertain
- Every narrative element should earn its place

# Completion Instructions
When this issue is complete:
1. STOP and notify the user
2. Tell the user to run /commit to save this work
3. Inform the user that ALL README refactoring issues are now complete

# Notes
- Be honest and critical
- Protect the reader's time
- Preserve what works, cut what doesn't
- The goal: technically excellent README that's also enjoyable to read
- Not too dry, not too fluffy - just right

title: Enhance presence endpoint with agent registration
description:
Current /v1/presence only discovers Saturn services via mDNS.

Future enhancement: Let agents register their presence so other agents know who's working.

Proposed flow:
1. Agent calls POST /v1/presence/register with agent_id, working_on (beads issue)
2. Service maintains active_agents dict with heartbeat timestamps
3. Other agents can query GET /v1/presence to see who's working
4. Agents timeout after 5 minutes without heartbeat

This enables factory floor awareness: 'Agent Beta is working on BD-42, Agent Gamma is doing code review.'

From Winter Memo: 'If Saturn provided a factory floor view—who's active, what they're working on—I could make better decisions.'

title: Consolidate beacon server into single file following Saturn server pattern
description:
Current beacon implementation is split across 4 files (333 lines total):
- beacons/jwt_manager.py (85 lines) - JWTManager class
- beacons/beacon_announcer.py (89 lines) - BeaconAnnouncer class  
- beacons/key_rotation.py (45 lines) - rotation_loop function
- beacons/deepinfra_beacon.py (114 lines) - Main server

This doesn't match the existing Saturn server pattern:
- servers/openrouter_server.py - 377 lines, all in one file
- servers/ollama_server.py - 344 lines, all in one file
- servers/fallback_server.py - 264 lines, all in one file

Consolidation Plan:
Merge all beacon server components into beacons/deepinfra_beacon.py as a single ~333 line file containing:
1. JWTManager class (from jwt_manager.py)
2. BeaconAnnouncer class (from beacon_announcer.py)
3. rotation_loop function (from key_rotation.py)
4. FastAPI app and main() (already in deepinfra_beacon.py)

Benefits:
- Follows established Saturn architecture pattern
- Reduces cognitive load (all beacon server logic in one place)
- Easier to understand and maintain
- Components are tightly coupled anyway (only used together)
- Still reasonable file size (~333 lines vs 264-377 for other servers)

Implementation:
1. Copy JWTManager class into deepinfra_beacon.py
2. Copy BeaconAnnouncer class into deepinfra_beacon.py
3. Copy rotation_loop function into deepinfra_beacon.py
4. Remove import statements for these modules
5. Delete jwt_manager.py, beacon_announcer.py, key_rotation.py
6. Update any tests that import these modules

Success Criteria:
- beacons/deepinfra_beacon.py runs standalone
- All functionality preserved
- No broken imports
- Follows same pattern as other Saturn servers
close_reason: Consolidated beacon server into single file (beacons/deepinfra_beacon.py). All functionality preserved, follows Saturn server pattern.

title: End-to-end integration testing
description:
Test complete beacon flow from startup through key rotation to expiration.

Test Scenarios:
1. Beacon Startup Flow:
   - Start beacon server
   - Verify mDNS announcement (dns-sd -B)
   - Verify TXT records contain ephemeral_key (dns-sd -L)
   
2. Client Discovery Flow:
   - Start test client
   - Verify discovery within 5 seconds
   - Verify key extraction
   - Verify successful API call to DeepInfra
   
3. Key Rotation (5 minute wait):
   - Observe beacon log rotation event
   - Observe client log update event
   - Save old key for comparison
   - Verify new key works
   
4. Key Expiration (10 minute wait):
   - Test old saved key (should be rejected by DeepInfra)
   - Test current key (should work)

Document all test results with timestamps and outcomes.

Success Criteria:
- All 8 success criteria from implementation plan verified
- Complete flow documented with evidence (logs, screenshots)
- No manual intervention needed after startup
notes: Testing framework provided via test_beacon_flow.py and beacon_test_client.py

title: Edge case testing and error handling
description:
Test edge cases and error conditions to ensure robust behavior.

Test Cases:
1. JWT >250 chars:
   - If token exceeds TXT record safe limit, document behavior
   - Test if truncation occurs
   - Document fallback strategy if needed
   
2. DeepInfra API rate limits:
   - Simulate rate limiting (429 errors)
   - Verify rotation thread handles gracefully
   - Verify exponential backoff or retry logic
   
3. Network failures during rotation:
   - Disconnect network mid-rotation
   - Verify beacon handles exception
   - Verify rotation retries when network returns
   
4. Multiple clients sharing same key:
   - Start 2+ clients discovering same beacon
   - Verify all get same ephemeral key
   - Verify all can make API calls
   
5. Client arrival mid-cycle:
   - Start beacon, wait 2 minutes
   - Start new client
   - Verify client gets current key (valid for 3+ more minutes)
   
6. Beacon crash recovery:
   - Kill beacon process
   - Verify clients detect removal
   - Restart beacon
   - Verify clients rediscover

Document all findings and mitigation strategies.

Success Criteria:
- All edge cases tested and documented
- Error handling verified
- Mitigation strategies identified
notes: Error handling implemented in rotation_loop.py, edge cases handled in code

title: Implement JWTManager class for ephemeral credential generation
description:
Create JWTManager class with thread-safe token storage and rotation detection.

Implementation:
- Create JWTManager class with threading.Lock for thread safety
- Implement generate_token() calling DeepInfra scoped JWT API
  - Headers: Authorization with DEEPINFRA_API_KEY
  - Payload: api_key_name='auto', expires_delta=600 (10 min)
  - Omit 'models' field (allows all models per Adam's requirement)
- Implement get_current_token() with lock
- Implement needs_rotation() checking if rotation interval (5 min) reached
- Store current_token and expires_at timestamp

Success Criteria:
- JWTManager generates valid tokens
- Thread-safe token access
- Rotation detection logic works (5 min interval with 10 min expiration buffer)
- Unit testable

title: Implement BeaconAnnouncer class with zeroconf mDNS registration
description:
Create BeaconAnnouncer class using python-zeroconf library for mDNS service registration with ephemeral key in TXT records.

Implementation:
- Create BeaconAnnouncer class using zeroconf library
- Implement register() method:
  - Create ServiceInfo for _saturn._tcp.local.
  - TXT records: version, api='DeepInfra', priority, ephemeral_key, rotation_interval, features
  - Add character count warning if ephemeral_key >240 chars
  - Call zeroconf.register_service()
- Implement unregister() for cleanup
  - Unregister service and close zeroconf instance
- Support re-registration (for key rotation): unregister then register

Success Criteria:
- Beacon appears in 'dns-sd -B _saturn._tcp local'
- TXT records visible in 'dns-sd -L <service> _saturn._tcp local'
- ephemeral_key present in TXT records
- Warning logged if key exceeds safe length

title: Implement key rotation background thread
description:
Create rotation_loop() function that runs in daemon thread to automatically rotate keys every 5 minutes.

Implementation:
- Create rotation_loop(jwt_manager, beacon_announcer) function
- Run in daemon thread (doesn't block shutdown)
- Check every 60 seconds if jwt_manager.needs_rotation()
- On rotation:
  1. Log rotation start
  2. jwt_manager.generate_token()
  3. beacon_announcer.register() (re-registers with new key)
  4. Log rotation complete
- Add exception handling:
  - Catch network failures gracefully
  - Catch DeepInfra API rate limits (429 errors)
  - Log errors but continue running

Success Criteria:
- Background thread starts successfully
- Observable key rotation every 5 minutes
- Old key replaced with new key in mDNS announcement
- Graceful error handling (network failures don't crash thread)

title: Implement BeaconListener class for service discovery
description:
Create BeaconListener(ServiceListener) class for discovering beacons and extracting ephemeral keys from TXT records.

Implementation:
- Create BeaconListener class extending ServiceListener
- Thread-safe beacon storage (dict with lock)
- Implement add_service(zc, type_, name):
  - Get service info
  - Extract ephemeral_key from TXT records
  - Extract priority, rotation_interval, url
  - Store in beacons dict
  - Log discovery with key preview (first 60 chars)
- Implement update_service(zc, type_, name):
  - Log update event
  - Call add_service to re-extract new key
- Implement remove_service(zc, type_, name):
  - Remove from beacons dict
  - Log removal
- Implement get_best_beacon():
  - Return lowest priority beacon
  - Return None if no beacons available

Success Criteria:
- Listener detects beacon within 5 seconds
- Extracts ephemeral_key correctly from TXT records
- Thread-safe beacon access
- Priority-based selection works

title: Implement beacon_test_client.py with direct DeepInfra API calls
description:
Create standalone test client that discovers beacons and calls DeepInfra API directly (NOT through beacon proxy).

Implementation:
- Create clients/beacon_test_client.py (NEW FILE - standalone test)
- Discovery setup:
  - Create BeaconListener instance
  - Create ServiceBrowser with zeroconf
  - Wait for beacon discovery (timeout 5 seconds)
- Implement chat_with_deepinfra(ephemeral_key, model, message):
  - POST to https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/chat/completions
  - Headers: Authorization: Bearer {ephemeral_key}
  - Payload: model, messages
  - Log request details (model, key preview)
  - Handle response and errors
- Main flow:
  1. Discover beacon
  2. Extract ephemeral key
  3. Make test API call
  4. Display response

Success Criteria:
- Client discovers beacon within 5 seconds
- Extracts ephemeral_key successfully
- Makes successful API call to DeepInfra (not through beacon)
- Response displayed correctly

title: README Storytelling: Merge Design Fictions
description:
# Objective
Take the existing design fiction (Derek and Sarah's story) and the new beacon design fiction, then integrate them into a cohesive narrative arc that keeps readers engaged throughout the README.

# Source Materials
- Current README.md (Derek/Sarah story, lines 9-28)

Create a merged narrative that:
1. Flows naturally from one story to the next
2. Builds on concepts introduced in earlier stories
3. Maintains consistent tone and voice
4. Uses storytelling to create natural transitions between technical sections
5. Keeps readers engaged without overwhelming them

# Guidelines
- Stories should complement each other, not compete
- Each story should introduce concepts that lead naturally into technical docs
- Maintain the "show, don't tell" approach
- Keep the overall narrative arc coherent
- Consider: What's the journey from "why Saturn?" to "why beacons?" to "let's try it"?

# Completion Instructions
When this issue is complete:
1. STOP and notify the user
2. Tell the user to run /commit to save this work
3. Inform the user that the next issue to work on is merging the design fiction with technical documentation

# Notes
- This is independent from technical planning (can be done in parallel)
- Focus on narrative flow and reader engagement
- The output should be a story arc, not the final README
- Think: "How do we guide readers from curiosity to understanding to action?"

title: Consolidate beacon client components into single file
description:
Current beacon client implementation is split across 2 files (210 lines total):
- clients/beacon_listener.py (96 lines) - BeaconListener class for discovery
- clients/beacon_test_client.py (114 lines) - Test client with chat_with_deepinfra()

BeaconListener is currently only used by beacon_test_client.py, making the split unnecessary.

Consolidation Plan:
Merge into clients/beacon_client.py as a single ~210 line file containing:
1. BeaconListener class (for reusability in other clients)
2. chat_with_deepinfra function (direct API call helper)
3. main() function (test/demo functionality)

Benefits:
- All beacon client logic in one place
- BeaconListener still reusable (other clients can import it)
- Simpler for users to understand and use
- Reduces file count from 2 to 1
- Reasonable file size (~210 lines)

Future Integration:
When integrating beacon discovery into existing Saturn clients (local_proxy_client.py, 
simple_chat_client.py, etc.), they can import BeaconListener from this file.

Implementation:
1. Create clients/beacon_client.py
2. Copy BeaconListener class from beacon_listener.py
3. Copy chat_with_deepinfra and main from beacon_test_client.py
4. Update imports
5. Delete beacon_listener.py and beacon_test_client.py
6. Update tests to use new module name

Success Criteria:
- clients/beacon_client.py runs standalone
- BeaconListener class can be imported by other clients
- All functionality preserved
- Test client works identically
close_reason: Consolidated beacon client into single file (clients/beacon_client.py). BeaconListener remains importable, all functionality preserved.

title: Design spawn protocol for subordinate agent delegation
description:
From Winter Memo: 'I can't delegate downward... a smaller, cheaper model should do grunt work.'

The spawn protocol would let agents request subordinate agents for repetitive tasks.

Questions to answer:
1. How would Claude Code spawn a subprocess with different model?
2. How do parent/child agents communicate? (Agent Mail? File-based?)
3. How does the subordinate report results back?
4. Cost tracking across spawned agents?

This is future work - requires more research into Claude Code internals and Agent Mail integration.

Related: Steve Yegge's multi-diver analogy - PM diver, coder diver, review diver instead of one big diver.

title: Research budget enforcement feasibility
description:
From Winter Memo: 'What if Saturn beacons had budgets instead of just access?'

Budget enforcement would require Saturn to intercept traffic (proxy model), which:
- Adds latency
- Makes Saturn a single point of failure
- Requires maintaining proxy infrastructure

Alternative approaches to explore:
1. Advisory only - show usage, let agents self-pace (current approach)
2. Client-side enforcement via MCP hook that refuses requests over budget
3. DeepInfra spending limits on scoped JWTs (if API supports it)
4. Modify Claude Code hooks to check budget before tool calls

This needs research to determine if enforcement is feasible without proxying.

Related: The beacon model (credential dispenser) vs server model (proxy) tradeoff.
